QF.id: AIFM AIFs in India and Suitability_2

question.text: Ms. Ananya Krishnan, Chief Investment Officer at Saraswati Capital, is structuring a new fund that will invest primarily in late-stage unlisted growth companies through equity and equity-linked instruments with no leverage at fund level. Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012, this fund MUST be registered as:

answer.text: Category I AIF — Venture Capital Fund sub-category
Category III AIF — because unlisted growth equity employs complex strategies
Category II AIF — Private Equity Fund
Specified AIF — because private equity is not a defined sub-category

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the AIF Managers workbook (pp. 82-87 and p. 487), Private Equity Funds invest primarily in equity and equity-linked instruments or partnership interests of investee companies, distinct from early-stage venture capital. Private Equity Funds fall under Category II AIF because they do not receive specific incentives from the government (which would make them Category I) and do not undertake complex or leveraged trading strategies (which would make them Category III). The Trap: Option A confuses later-stage Private Equity with early-stage Venture Capital, which is a Category I sub-category. Option B wrongly assumes that unlisted growth equity is Category III; Category III is defined by complex or leveraged trading strategies, not by investing in unlisted growth equity. Option D misuses the Specified AIF concept; Private Equity Fund is a defined Category II construct in the source. Note: Private Equity Funds invest primarily in equity, equity-linked instruments or partnership interests of investee companies and are registered as Category II, as set out on pp. 82-87 and p. 487 of the source.
